title: Anemic Domain Model
pattern: Structs representing domain concepts are designed as passive data containers with public fields and no behavior, while all validation and business rules are placed in stateless services.
why_bad: It defeats the primary benefit of object-oriented/module encapsulation. Business invariants cannot be protected because any caller can mutate the entity's fields directly into invalid states, leaving the code prone to inconsistency.
detection: Domain structs containing only public fields and zero impl blocks, while business logic resides entirely in separate helper/service classes.
counterexample: Pure data structures (like standard DTOs or config structs) that do not represent complex business entities with invariants.
fix: Keep fields private, and encapsulate mutation operations inside methods on the domain struct itself (e.g., `invoice.pay()`), ensuring invariants are verified.
source: Eric Evans, *Domain-Driven Design* (2003), Chapter 4 ("Isolating the Domain"); Vaughn Vernon, *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* (2013), Chapter 10.
